node.title: Re^4: How to pass a folder name to Windows external commands?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I'm using 'dir' in an attempt to glob a filespec and get Unicode filenames

I see, that does make it a bit more complicated. I used [mod://Win32::LongPath] in the following, plus [mod://Text::Glob] since you mentioned globs, but of course using a regex directly would be easier.

use warnings;
use strict;
use utf8;
use Text::Glob 'glob_to_regex';
use Win32::LongPath;
use File::Spec::Functions qw/no_upwards catfile/;
use IPC::Run3 'run3';
use Data::Dump;

my $glob = glob_to_regex('*Перл*');
my $dir = "C:\\Temp\\testuni";

my $dh = Win32::LongPath->new;
$dh->opendirL($dir) or die "unable to open $dir: $^E";
for my $file ( grep {/$glob/} no_upwards $dh->readdirL ) {
	my $path = catfile($dir, $file);
	my $sp = shortpathL($path);
	run3 ['hex', $sp], undef, \my $out;
	dd $path, $sp, $out;
}
$dh->closedirL;
Is 'hex' a command in your example?

I happened to have C:\Windows\hex.exe lying around, a simple hex dump tool from [https://github.com/hollasch/hex|here].

Is there a reason that you used short pathnames?

In my [id://11141828|first example], that's just how [mod://Path::Class] returned them; in my example above I used them because it appeared to be easier to pass the pathname to the external command that way.

I'm using robocopy /l to get the total size of a folder, including subfolders. It's supposed to be a fast way to do that.

I tried running robocopy, and at least on my system the report it outputs doesn't mention file sizes anywhere. You might also want to look at e.g. the Perl version of [https://metacpan.org/dist/PerlPowerTools/source/bin/du|du] to see the algorithm used there.

I tried using run3, but I don't understand its rules and haven't got it working yet.

Again, it would be best if you can show an [id://1177642|SSCCE].
